history.text: Vacated after Ultimate Warrior won the WWF Championship at WrestleMania VI; a tournament later crowned Mr. Perfect.
Unified into the Intercontinental Championship at Survivor Series 2001, leaving the US title inactive.
Following the first brand split, the title became exclusive to Raw.
The WWF was renamed WWE.
Unified with the European Championship in a ladder match won by Rob Van Dam.
Moved to SmackDown!.
Returned to Raw after Rob Van Dam defeated Chris Benoit.
Hardcore Championship unified into the Intercontinental Championship.
Triple H defeated Kane at No Mercy, unifying the two titles.
The Intercontinental Championship was deactivated after the unification.
Reactivated on Raw by co-general manager Stone Cold Steve Austin; Christian won the battle royal to claim it.
Rey Mysterio was drafted to SmackDown, moving the title there.
WWE did not recognize Kofi Kingston's tournament win; Drew McIntyre was still recognized as champion until Over the Limit.
The brand split was discontinued and the champion could appear on both brands.
The brand split was reintroduced and the title moved to SmackDown in the 2016 draft.
Dean Ambrose moved the title to Raw in the 2017 Superstar Shake-up.
Finn Bálor moved the title to SmackDown in the 2019 Superstar Shake-up.
Recognized as a third secondary title when NXT moved to USA Network.
Vacated after Sami Zayn refrained from competing during the COVID-19 pandemic; a tournament followed on SmackDown.
Recognition reversed when NXT returned to being WWE's developmental brand.
Gunther was drafted to Raw, moving the title back to Raw.
